title: Medicines and medical devices are being scored against a food nutrition sheet
status: proposal — schemas/ is frozen by a snapshot test, so this is NOT applied
problem: grocery's category "Health & supplements" holds 11,128 records and is scored against a 36-field food nutrition spec sheet. Roughly half of them are licensed medicines (a strip of 10 tablets, a dry syrup, a metered-dose inhaler) and a further 571 are devices and PPE (N95 masks, hot water bags, contact lenses). Neither will ever have energy_kcal_100g, nova_group, palm_oil or serving_size. The category fills at 19.93% against a grocery domain average of 39.65%, and the shortfall is almost entirely these two populations being asked food questions.

measured.note: No attribute value is removed by this change. E7 validates attributes against the domain's `fields` dictionary, not against a category's `spec`, so a nutrition value already recorded on a medicine stays on the record and stays valid; it simply stops being a question the medicine's product page asks. 285 recorded values move out of the counted slots this way, out of 79,836.

classification.principle: Every rule reads the product NAME. Manufacturer identity is deliberately NOT a rule: Cipla sells both Telmiget and a protein shake, so brand alone would misfile both directions.

rules_in_priority_order.rule: drug molecule / drug class / disease word
rules_in_priority_order.why: Food labelling law does not permit a molecule name or a disease claim on a supplement.

'strip of N', dry syrup, oral suspension, respules, rotacaps, metered-dose inhaler, eye/ear/nasal drops. Checked BEFORE food vocabulary so a flavoured paediatric cough syrup reads as the medicine it is.
'Medicated' or a % strength turns a soap or shampoo into a drug product (Ketocip 2% Shampoo).
A mg/mcg/IU strength on a hard dosage form with no food vocabulary anywhere in the name.
Masks, bandages, hot water bags, contact lenses, pepper spray, thermometers. Neither food nor medicine.

Whey, creatine, gummies, ashwagandha, shilajit, a named vitamin or mineral. This is what keeps 'Fish Oil 1000 mg' and 'HealthAid 500 mg Calcium Supplement' out of medicines — a bare mg number is NOT evidence of a drug.

Medicines.why_required_is_unchanged: Keeping required at ['quantity'] means no record becomes an E6 error on the move. Only 3 of the 5,139 medicines lack quantity and all 3 are already status:candidate.

Medical devices.why: A mask, a crepe bandage and a hot water bag answer pack, maker and origin questions, and nothing else on the food sheet.

fields_this_needs.note: Both proposed spec sheets are built ONLY from fields already declared in schemas/grocery.json, so this proposal adds no new field and cannot retype, narrow or drop an existing one. The ideal medicine sheet would also ask composition, strength, dosage form, prescription-required and marketing licence — those are five NEW fields and a larger change; they are deliberately left out of this proposal so the category move can be judged on its own.

blockers: schemas/grocery.json is frozen: src/schemas.test.ts asserts every domain's `required` map against src/required.snapshot.json. Adding the two categories adds two keys to the grocery map, so src/required.snapshot.json must be updated in the same commit. The test's own failure message sanctions exactly this.
Until the schema declares the categories, moving a record to "Medicines" is an E5 error ('category is not declared'). So the reclassification cannot be applied before the schema change is accepted.

unclear.why: No decisive signal in the name. Includes Ayurvedic proprietary medicines ('Himalaya Tentex Forte Tablets') that are genuinely hard to call without the pack.

cosmetic.why: Grooming products. About 23 of them are antifungal shampoos and soaps whose brand stems (Ketocip, Zocon, Candidox) are drugs, but naming them needs a brand-stem list I could not verify without fetching, so they stay put.

topical-relief.why: OTC counter-irritant rubs, balms and roll-ons (Moov, Zandu Balm, Volini). Drugs by licence in India but they read as personal care; they deserve their own decision rather than being forced either way.

review_2026_09_06.verdict: The classification work is sound and the schema change is the right call, but the proposed Medicines spec sheet is wrong: it carries food fields that medicines do not have, and omits medicine fields the source pages publish on 100% of pages.

proposed_sheet_measured.on: 3,601 records whose name states an Rx dosage form
proposed_sheet_measured.dead_fields: fssai_licence 0 of 3,601 (a medicine carries a DRUG licence, not an FSSAI one), allergens 0, additives 0, packaging_type 1, ingredients_order 5, preservatives 5, artificial_colours 5, artificial_flavours 5, marketed_by 13, shelf_life 22.

what_the_source_actually_publishes.note: Medicine pages carry a different attribute vocabulary entirely. None of them has a nutrition panel or an FSSAI number. These appear on 100% of pages and the repo captures none of them:

usable.Prescription required: 3,269 Yes / 203 No — arguably the single most important fact about a medicine

rejected_as_placeholders.Shelf Life (In days): 36500 — one hundred years — on 3,459 of 3,472 pages. A placeholder, the same failure mode as Blinkit's '1 g' Standard Serve Size. Do not read it.
rejected_as_placeholders.intake_per_dose: '1' on all 3,469 pages that carry it, so it is a default and not a fact.
rejected_as_placeholders.Pharma license needed: 'DL' on 3,454 of 3,472 — near-constant, so it distinguishes nothing.

review_2026_09_06.recommendation: Keep the two new categories, but build the Medicines sheet from what a medicine actually declares rather than from the food sheet's leftovers. That needs new FIELDS (prescription_required, dosage_form, drug_sensitivity), which is a larger schema decision than adding two categories -- and it turns this from 'ask fewer questions to raise the percentage' into 'ask the right questions', which is the difference that matters here.
review_2026_09_06.caution: A 5-field sheet of only what is already filled reaches 87.3%, but adopting it for that reason would be trimming the sheet to flatter the number. The case for dropping fssai_licence and the nutrition fields is that medicines do not have them -- verified on the pages -- not that they are empty.

second_source_corroboration_2026_09_07.why_it_matters: The proposal rested on 3,472 cached Blinkit pages. A second, independent source now reports the same conclusion, and supplies two facts Blinkit does not: the active pharmaceutical ingredient and the drug schedule.
second_source_corroboration_2026_09_07.field_coverage_measured: On the first 140 records banked, per the crawler's own facts.jsonl rather than a projection:
second_source_corroboration_2026_09_07.the_asymmetry_that_decides_it: The fields requiring a schema change are the COMPLETE ones — Rx status, drug schedule, dosage form and route are on every page. The one fact storable today without a schema change, the active ingredient in the top-level `ingredients` array, is the SPARSEST at 87 of 140. So the schema decision is not a refinement of this crawl; it is what determines whether the crawl's main product can be kept at all.
second_source_corroboration_2026_09_07.projected: ~2,100 usable records of the 4,162, each carrying an Rx status and a drug schedule. The final measured figure will be reported from the artefact, not this projection — an earlier cumulative counter misled at 60%, then 40%, then 52%.
second_source_corroboration_2026_09_07.safety_record_of_the_match: Only 5 of 4,162 records carry a GTIN, so the join is brand + qualifiers + strength + dosage form, all four required. Caught by the page-side strength re-check rather than the name match: Thyronorm 125mcg against a page reading 12.5mcg — a TENFOLD levothyroxine error — and Met XL 25mg against 0.25mg, hundredfold. Refused by the name rule: Methycobal vs Methycobal D, Telmiget 40mg vs Telmiget LN, Amcard 5mg vs Amcard At, Isryl M3 Forte vs m2 Forte, and New Erythrocin 250 mg, whose stem 'new' would have matched a Dyson hair dryer.
second_source_corroboration_2026_09_07.a_new_placeholder_pattern: Some Netmeds pages emit schema.org @type 'Product' rather than 'Drug', and on those `availableStrength` is present but holds an UNRENDERED MUSTACHE TEMPLATE — '{{product.attributes.genericnamewithdosage}}'. The page emits Product precisely because the drug attributes are absent. Widening the extractor to accept Product would have written literal {{...}} into ingredients on medicine records. Same class as Blinkit's '1 g' serve size and its 36500-day shelf life: a present field name is not a present fact.
second_source_corroboration_2026_09_07.CORRECTION_rx_is_not_evidence_here: My commit presented 'rx 140/140' as corroboration. It is not. The population was SELECTED on prescription dosage forms (strip of N, or an N mg/mcg strength), so the field is constant on this slice by construction — read directly from facts.jsonl at 197 records it is 197/197 'https://schema.org/PrescriptionOnly'. A field must not be justified on a sample chosen to make it look constant. The evidence that prescription status VARIES is Blinkit's 3,269 Yes / 889 No across a broader population, which was already in this file. The subagent caught this in its own result; I had not.

what_this_source_DOES_independently_show.legal_status varies and is unobtainable: Schedule H 179, Schedule NP 11, Schedule H1 7 at 197 records. Schedule H1 is the narcotic/antibiotic-restricted class, so this distinguishes products with different legal handling. Blinkit publishes a Schedule field too, but the active ingredient alongside it is what makes the pairing useful.
what_this_source_DOES_independently_show.the active ingredient: generic 183/186, active 121/186 — Blinkit does not publish this at all.
what_this_source_DOES_independently_show.dosage_form needs normalising: arrives in MIXED CASE — TABLET 149, Tablet 22, CAPSULE 23, Capsule 3. It needs a controlled vocabulary and case folding, or it will carry two spellings of one value. Recorded before anything is written.

what_the_merge_is_actually_worth.the_arithmetic: `ingredients` is a TOP-LEVEL field, not a member of any category's spec sheet, so a value written there does not count toward fill at all. Only `manufacturer` and `marketed_by` are spec slots in Health & supplements.
what_the_merge_is_actually_worth.headroom: Of the 4,162 medicine-signal records, 2,714 lack manufacturer and 4,064 lack marketed_by. At the crawl's measured 86% usable rate over 2,516 matches, the upper bound on new spec-counted values is about 4,063 — roughly **0.13 percentage points** of overall fill.
what_the_merge_is_actually_worth.why_it_is_still_worth_doing: The ~2,000 active ingredients are the most useful fact in the set and the reason the crawl exists: they say what a medicine IS. They simply are not scored, because the field that can hold them today is outside the spec sheet. That is another way of stating the case for the schema change — the catalogue cannot currently count the best fact it holds about a medicine.
what_the_merge_is_actually_worth.honesty_note: Anyone reading a fill delta after this merge should expect ~0.1 points, not a jump. The value is in what the records say, not in the percentage.
